steps.description:
Read up the notes on CLASS.

Click here to view the notes.

The instructor will then brief you on the topic.

Create a python class named Friend with the following attributes.

Object Variable: name stores name of a friend

Function: display() displays the name

When an object is created from the class, it will initialise variable name.

Write a program to ask the user to input a friend's name. Create an object from the class and initialise its name, then call the function to display the name.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

Jason Momoa

Chris Evans

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter name: Jason Momoa Jason Momoa

Example 2 Enter name: Chris Evans Chris Evans

Create a python class named Bird with the following attributes:

Object Variables species stores the species name colour stores the colour name

Function display() displays the species and colour

Write a program to ask the user to input the species and colour of a bird. Create an object from the class and initialise its variables, then call its function to display the information.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

eagle white

owl brown

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Input bird species: eagle Input bird colour: white white eagle

Example 2 Input bird species: owl Input bird colour: brown brown owl

Create a python class named Number with the following attributes.

Object Variable num_list stores a list of integers

Function display() displays the first and last integers in a row

When an object is created from the class, it will ask user to input a list of integers in a row and initialise variable num_list with the values.

Write a program to perform the following: 1. Create an object from the class. 2. Call display().

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - Other than initialising, __init__() is also like a normal function where you can execute commands such as input()

Test Input

5 9 4 7 2

1 0 3 5 7 2 0

5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter a list of integers: 5 9 4 7 2 5 2

Example 2 Enter a list of integers: 1 0 3 5 7 2 0 1 0

Example 3 Enter a list of integers: 5 5 5

Create a python class named Number with the following attributes.

Object Variable num_list stores a list of integers

Functions display() displays all the numbers in a row add(n) adds n to each number in the list

When an object is created from the class, it will ask user to input a list of integers in a row and initialise variable num_list with the values.

Write a program to perform the following: 1. Create an object from the class. 2. Call display(). 3. Call add(5). 4. Call display(). 5. Call add(-3). 6. Call display().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

5 9 4 7 2

1 0 3 5 7 2 0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter a list of integers: 5 9 4 7 2 5 9 4 7 2 10 14 9 12 7 7 11 6 9 4

Example 2 Enter a list of integers: 1 0 3 5 7 2 0 1 0 3 5 7 2 0 6 5 8 10 12 7 5 3 2 5 7 9 4 2
